# bob records

List, inspect, check, create, and update Record Notes

```text title="bob records --help"
List, inspect, check, create, and update Record Notes

Bare `bob records` runs the read-only list. `new` creates a note through the shared records planner and refuses missing fields or duplicates. `update` edits an existing note in place.

Usage: bob records [COMMAND]

Commands:
  check   Check Record Notes against their album schemas
  list    List Record Note collections (default)
  new     Create one Record Note from its schema
  show    Show one record schema and its common values
  update  Update one existing Record Note in place

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Bare `bob records` runs the read-only list.

Examples:
  bob records                                      List record types and counts
  bob records show restaurant                     Inspect a schema and common values
  bob records check -f json                       Lint every record folder
  bob records new restaurant 'Ramen Nagi' -s status=to_try

See docs/records.md for the schema, CLI, and lint contract.
Run 'bob records <command> --help' for more information on a command.
```

## bob records check

Check Record Notes against their album schemas

```text title="bob records check --help"
Lint each record folder from the effective vault's album notes. Checks the type link, parent membership, required and typed fields, legacy keys, checkboxes, and records filed outside their folder. TYPE accepts a noun or album stem.

Usage: bob records check [OPTIONS] [TYPE]

Arguments:
  [TYPE]
          Record noun or album stem

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <PATH>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

Examples:
  bob records check
  bob records check restaurant
  bob records check eat
  bob records check -f json

See docs/records.md for the schema and lint rules.
```

## bob records list

List Record Note collections (default)

```text title="bob records list --help"
Show each album record type, its folder, note count, and required fields. Invalid albums still contribute their folder counts. This command is read-only. Bare `bob records` runs this command.

Usage: bob records list [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <PATH>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

Examples:
  bob records
  bob records list
  bob records list -f json

See docs/records.md for record schemas.
```

## bob records new

Create one Record Note from its schema

```text title="bob records new --help"
Plan and create a single Record Note. TYPE accepts a noun or album stem. Supply fields with repeated --set KEY=VALUE arguments and notes with repeated --note arguments. Missing required fields are refused with a ready-to-copy draft. --dry-run prints the exact Markdown without writing.

Usage: bob records new [OPTIONS] <TYPE> <TITLE>

Arguments:
  <TYPE>
          Record noun or album stem

  <TITLE>
          Title of the new record note

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <PATH>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -d, --dry-run
          Print the planned note without writing

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

  -n, --note <TEXT>
          Append a note bullet; may be repeated

  -o, --open
          Open the created note in Obsidian

  -s, --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Set a configured field; may be repeated

  -S, --stem <STEM>
          Use an explicit filename stem

Examples:
  bob records new restaurant 'Ramen Nagi' -s status=to_try -s category=Ramen -s location=Clark
  bob records new eat 'Ramen Nagi' -s status=to_try -s category=Ramen -s location=Clark
  bob records new podcast 'The Daily' -s status=to_try -s category=News -n 'Recommended by Kelly' -d
  bob records new restaurant '1950 Originals' -S 1950s_originals -s status=to_try -s category=Pizza -s location=Westwood
  bob records new restaurant 'Ninja Sushi' -d -f json

See docs/records.md for field kinds, defaults, and failure behavior.
```

```text title="bob records show --help"
          Output format: human or json

          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

Examples:
  bob records show restaurant
  bob records show eat
  bob records show podcast -f json

See docs/records.md for the schema contract.
```

## bob records update

Update one existing Record Note in place

```text title="bob records update --help"
Resolve an existing record by TYPE and STEM, then edit only the supplied YAML value spans and append notes with repeated --note arguments. TYPE accepts a noun or album stem. Field-only and note-only updates work without repeating required creation fields. --dry-run prints the exact Markdown without writing.

Usage: bob records update [OPTIONS] <TYPE> <STEM>

Arguments:
  <TYPE>
          Record noun or album stem

  <STEM>
          Existing filename stem of the record note

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <PATH>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -d, --dry-run
          Print the planned note without writing

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

  -n, --note <TEXT>
          Append a note bullet; may be repeated

  -o, --open
          Open the updated note in Obsidian

  -s, --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Set a configured field; may be repeated

Examples:
  bob records update restaurant ninja_sushi -s status=liked -n 'Went back, still great'
  bob records update eat ninja_sushi -s status=liked
  bob records update restaurant ninja_sushi -s location= -d
  bob records update podcast talk_python -n 'Listened to the async episode' -d -f json

See docs/records.md for update semantics, optional clearing, and failure behavior.
```
